native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: At HIGH socioeconomic levels is the Black students' completion-rate deficit (relative to White and other students) least pronounced / the White-minus-Black completion gap smallest, though it never becomes an actual Black advantage.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Bucketed SES into global terciles and quartiles; computed P(BA=1) per race x SES level with n, event counts, Wilson 95% CI widths. 2) Defined the comparison as the gap in percentage points: White-minus-Black, pooled-other-minus-Black, Hispanic-minus-Black at each SES level. 3) Tested significance via logistic regression P(BA) ~ continuous SES x race (baseline White) with an LR test on the interaction terms. 4) Sensitivity: terciles vs quartiles vs continuous interaction; White vs pooled-other baselines; a model adjusted for ability (ASVAB composite) and class percentile (interpretation only); and within-race SES terciles as a secondary lens (flagged as unequal absolute SES). 5) All headline claims are descriptive, with the significant interaction reported explicitly and sparsity (236 events, single-digit Black top-SES cells) kept visible.

sub_hypo.text: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels, indicated by a significant positive SES × is_Black interaction coefficient of 0.6271.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background factors and academic resources recorded at secondary school graduation.
sub_hypo.relations: The BA degree completion advantage for Black students increases with SES, as indicated by a significant positive interaction between SES and Black race status (SES × is_Black coefficient: 0.6271).

sub_hypo.text: Black students' BA completion-rate deficit relative to White and other students is smallest at high socioeconomic levels, but never becomes a Black completion-rate advantage.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants, comparing racial differences in BA completion across socioeconomic levels, with emphasis on high SES. SES levels are defined primarily by global terciles and quartiles; within-race terciles are secondary and represent unequal absolute SES. Claims are descriptive, with sparse Black top-SES cells.
sub_hypo.relations: SES moderates the association between race and BA completion: White-minus-Black, pooled-other-minus-Black, and Hispanic-minus-Black completion-rate gaps in percentage points are smallest at high SES, without reversing into a Black advantage. The workflow reports a significant continuous SES-by-race interaction in logistic regression with White as the baseline. Ability and class percentile are adjustment variables in a sensitivity model used for interpretation only.
